answer: At each summit of the network, agents are randomly assigned to a juror oasis where a ferrous‑weighted stake is locked; the stake size scales with the number of identities an agent controls. Jurors periodically audit a subset of graded transactions, and any discrepancy forces the loss of the locked stake and removal of the offending identities. An attacker must therefore purchase proportional ferrous collateral for every fake node and risk total forfeiture on each spot‑check, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
